480	steered the ship wherever he wanted. He told him: now go right, go left, turn
481	right, right again, left again, stop, drop anchor. They dropped the
482	anchor. He said: bring me a bucket. They brought a bucket, lowered the bucket
483	into the water and pulled up a bucket of water. The
484	elderly Kabbalist, Rav Kaduri, said to them: now each one take a cup of this water.
485	This is the well of Miriam. Drink, so that you become like a strengthening spring.
486	We said the blessing "shehakol nihyah bidvaro". Those who were thirsty did; if you're not thirsty, you don't bless.
487	We said "shehakol nihyah bidvaro" and drank it all, each one took a cup for himself, which was
488	two revi'iyot, and we drank. I asked him: so how was the taste of
489	the water? Did you think of something else? He says to me: I didn't know you could think of something else. So it stayed the taste of
490	water. Nobody knew this, because at least I had a sign to show whether it was really so, since the Rav Chida writes that if
491	you think of the taste of something else, another drink, it is the taste of that drink, and if you think of nothing, it is the taste of
492	water. They didn't think of anything, so it would be the taste of water. So I asked him: so,
493	Chacham Moshe, and do you remember since then everything you learn?
494	So he said to me: HaShem have mercy on us. I didn't understand what this answer is, this "have mercy".
495	Does he remember or not?
496	What is "HaShem have mercy", or doesn't have mercy?
497	I said, maybe he says this out of humility?
498	Maybe he doesn't want to tell?
499	I said to him: what is "HaShem have mercy"?
500	He says: HaShem have mercy on us.
501	Okay, I understood.
502	From that day I kept an eye on him in the yeshivah.
503	I said I would check on him, to see whether it truly stayed with them or did not stay with them.
504	And then I would come and ask him all kinds of questions.
505	Like that, not, God forbid, to test him.
506	Just to see.
507	Not to test.
508	To check.
509	And then I asked him, and apparently it truly did not stay with them.
510	So what will you say, that Rav Kaduri brought them just water to drink?
511	I don't think so.
512	So how can this be?
513	Rather, what?
514	The water that brings a person memory is only an aid, only an addition, but it does not
515	make you remember completely.
516	And therefore, if all kinds of things arise afterward, like the passing of time, or anger, or situations of pressure,
517	it could be that the water truly will not help, and therefore they said "I forgot".
518	And this may be the reason how Moshe Rabbeinu forgot.
519	Why?
